blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
In 1995 Kashaev introduced a complex valued link invariant for an integer $N\ge 2$ by using the quantum dilogarithm [@Kashaev:MODPLA95] and then he observed that his invariant grows exponentially with growth rate proportional to the volume of the knot complement for several hyperbolic knots [@Kashaev:LETMP97]. He also conjectured that this also holds for any hyperbolic knot, where a knot in the three-sphere is called hyperbolic if its complement possesses a complete hyperbolic structure with finite volume.

blocks.title: Link invariant from a Yang–Baxter operator
blocks.content:
In general we conjecture that this is also true, that is, for any knot the asymptotic
behavior of the colored Jones polynomial would determine the volume of a three-
manifold obtained as the deformation associated with the parameter u.
The aim of this article is to give an elementary introduction to these conjectures
including many examples so that nonexperts can easily understand. I hope you will
join us.

Yang–Baxter operator

Alexander's theorem (Theorem [\[thm:Alexander\]](#thm:Alexander){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:Alexander"}) and Markov's theorem (Theorem [\[thm:Markov\]](#thm:Markov){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:Markov"}) can be used to define link invariants. I will follow Turaev [@Turaev:INVEM88] to introduce a link invariant derived from a Yang-Baxter operator.

Let $V$ be an $N$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{C}$, $R$ an isomorphism from $V\otimes V$ to itself, $m$ an isomorphism from $V$ to itself, and $a$ and $b$ non-zero complex numbers.

blocks.title: Quantum (g,V) invariant
blocks.content:
One of the important ways to construct an enhanced Yang--Baxter operator is to use a quantum group, which is a deformation of a Lie algebra.

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a Lie algebra. Then one can define a quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$ as a deformation of $\mathfrak{g}$ with $q$ a complex parameter ([@Drinfeld:ICM86], [@Jimbo:LETMP1985]). Given a representation $\rho\colon\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{gl}(V)$ of $\mathfrak{g}$ one can construct an enhanced Yang--Baxter operator. The corresponding invariant is called the quantum $(\mathfrak{g},V)$ invariant. For details see [@Turaev:INVEM88].

blocks.title: Example of calculation
Volume conjecture
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Volume_Conjecture label="sec:Volume_Conjecture"}

In this section we state the Volume Conjecture and then prove it for the figure-eight knot. We also give supporting evidence for the conjecture.

blocks.title: Statement of the Volume Conjecture
blocks.content:
In [@Kashaev:MODPLA95] Kashaev introduced a link invariant $\langle L\rangle_N\in\mathbb{C}$ for an integer $N$ greater than one and a link $L$ by using the quantum dilogarithm. Then he observed in [@Kashaev:LETMP97] that the limit $2\pi\lim_{N\to\infty}\log|\langle K\rangle_N|/N$ is equal to the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement if a knot $K$ is hyperbolic. Here a knot in the three-sphere $S^3$ is called hyperbolic if its complement possesses a complete hyperbolic structure with finite volume. He also conjectured this would also hold for any hyperbolic knot.

blocks.title: Proof of the Volume Conjecture for the figure-eight knot
Knots and links for which the Volume Conjecture is proved
blocks.content:
As far as I know the Volume Conjecture is proved for

1.  figure-eight knot by Ekholm,

2.  $5_2$ knot by Kashaev and Yokota,

3.  Whitehead doubles of torus knots by Zheng [@Zheng:CHIAM22007],

4.  torus knots by Kashaev and Tirkkonen [@Kashaev/Tirkkonen:ZAPNS2000],

5.  torus links of type $(2,2m)$ by Hikami [@Hikami:COMMP2004],

6.  knots and links with volume zero by van der Veen [@van_der_veen:2008],

7.  Borromean rings by Garoufalidis and Lê [@Garoufalidis/Le:2005],

8.  twisted Whitehead links by Zheng [@Zheng:CHIAM22007],

9.  Whitehead chains by van der Veen [@van_der_Veen:ACTMV2009]

blocks.title: Supporting evidence for the Volume Conjecture
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:VC_proof label="sec:VC_proof"}

The Volume Conjecture is proved only for several knots and links but I think it is true possibly with some modification; for example we may need to replace the limit with the limit superior (see [@van_der_Veen:ACTMV2009 Conjecture 2]). In this section I will explain why I think it is true.

::: remark
Descriptions in this section are *not rigorous*.
:::

blocks.title: Generalizations of the Volume Conjecture
blocks.content: []{#sec:generalization label="sec:generalization"} In this section we consider generalizations of the Volume Conjecture.

blocks.title: Complexification
blocks.content:
In [@Thurston:BULAM31982] W. Thurston pointed out that the Chern--Simons invariant [@Chern/Simons:ANNMA21974] can be regarded as an imaginary part of the volume. Neumann and Zagier gave a precise conjecture [@Neumann/Zagier:TOPOL85 Conjecture, p. 309] which was proved to be true by Yoshida [@Yoshida:INVEM85]. For combinatorial approaches to the Chern--Simons invariant, see [@Neumann1992] and [@Zickert:DUKMJ2009].

So it would be natural to drop the absolute value sign of the left hand side of the Volume Conjecture and add the Chern--Simons invariant to the right hand side.

blocks.title: Deformation of the parameter
blocks.content:
In the Volume Conjecture (Conjecture [\[conj:VC\]](#conj:VC){reference-type="ref" reference="conj:VC"}) and its complexification (Conjecture [\[conj:CVC\]](#conj:CVC){reference-type="ref" reference="conj:CVC"}), the (possible) limit corresponds to the complete hyperbolic structure of $S^3\setminus{K}$ for a hyperbolic knot $K$. As described in [@Thurston:GT3M Chapter 4] the complete structure can be deformed to incomplete ones.
